title: Information flows first from the anatomical loop to single-cell energy

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Information flows first from the anatomical loop to single-cell energy

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, transfer entropy from energy to cell state peaks before the reverse flow, indicating that information is first driven by the tissue-level anatomical homeostatic loop, which then controls the energy cells need to survive; the authors take this to suggest top-down information is key to manipulating tissue dynamics.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, in our scheme, the information was first driven by the anatomical loop, and the energy needed for single-cell survival was controlled by this loop.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-11: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The simulation and temporal ordering can be reproduced from public code using standard information-theoretic analysis. Existing outputs discriminate directionality less well than they discriminate top-down causation, so the interpretation is weaker than the numerical result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rerun the model and compare the time of the peak transfer entropy from energy to cell state with the reverse direction across seeds and controllers. The timing result is confirmed if the reported ordering is robust, but the top-down interpretation additionally requires interventions on tissue state.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A tissue-level variable and a top-down rival must be specified independently.

Transfer entropy is predictive rather than necessarily causal.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The peak-order comparison can be rerun once energy and state are logged from the public model, using the paper's definition of local transfer entropy. The deposited code does not include those logs or the winner network, and the further statement that the anatomical loop controls single-cell energy is not identified by peak order alone. A re-evolved tissue can test the qualitative order, not the published figure.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Average local transfer entropy from each cell's energy to its state, and the reverse, across the tissue time series. An energy-to-state peak near step 55 that precedes overlap of the two directions would confirm the reported order; a first peak in the opposite direction, or simultaneous rise, would refute the order.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A lead of energy-to-state transfer entropy is compatible with a common driver and does not establish top-down control of survival energy.

Saved energy and state traces for the reported run are not in the code repository.
